In this section from *Clarity and Calm*, the master explains: *"Boundaries of Time All this skilful effort pays off by giving you more time to calm and clarify your mind."*. From the perspective of the Four Noble Truths, suffering arises whenever the mind grasps at impermanent phenomena (*anicca*) as a reliable self (*atta*). By establishing clear comprehension (*sampajañña*) and seeing conditioned events as empty of inherent ownership, craving (*taṇhā*) is unhooked. It is like grasping a poisonous cobra by the tail: tempting and sleek from afar, but deadly the moment you grasp it. Release the tail and live in safety. Anchor your understanding in direct seeing rather than speculative theory.
